newsitem.title: CHINA: Tonga athlete fined for beating HK buttock-fondler.
newsitem.headline: Tonga athlete fined for beating HK buttock-fondler.

text.p: South Pacific rugby star Isi Tu'ivai was fined US$380 for beating unconscious a Hong Kong restaurant chef he accused of fondling his fiancee's bottom --although the judge said the cook deserved a thrashing.

The 26-year-old Tu'ivai, from Tonga, a 1.8 metre (six feet) tall, 90 kg (198 pounds) Hong Kong fitness trainer and rugby player, admitted wounding cook Carl Duggan after a quarrel at the Joe Bananas bar in the Wanchai nightlife district in May.
Tu'ivai went bananas when he saw Duggan, 25, touch his girlfriend's bottom and punched the chef in the head, a court heard. Duggan fled but Tu'ivai chased and beat him unconscious.
Duggan denied touching 32-year-old Maria Rice, whom Tu'ivai is marrying in England later this month.
The chef suffered a broken jaw and needed 40 stitches.
But magistrate James Lee refused to order Tu'ivai to pay compensation, the South China Morning Post said.

"Wounding is normally a serious offence, but in this case I can only say the man asked for it. This is the price he pays for his behaviour," the magistrate, quoted by the newspaper, said. Duggan plans to sue for compensation in a civil lawsuit.
